qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Owns low-cost Saskatchewan potash mining infrastructure and an extensive North American ag retail network, but operates as a price-taker in global wholesale commodity fertilizer markets. Earnings fluctuate wildly with spot potash and nitrogen prices. 5-year normalized GAAP ROIC (~8-9%) fails the 12% hurdle. Major structural threat from BHP's US$14B+ Jansen mega-project adding 8.5 Mtpa (~10% of global supply).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). World-scale Saskatchewan potash producer and North American ag retailer rejected due to extreme commodity price-taker earnings volatility, sub-hurdle normalized ROIC (~8-9%), and long-term pricing headwinds from BHP's massive Jansen supply additions.
qualitative.evidence: Nutrien's earnings are driven by commodity fertilizer benchmarks (potash, ammonia, urea). Post-2022 windfall normalization has compressed GAAP ROIC to ~9%, failing the 12% hurdle. The company has no ability to raise prices above inflation independently of global commodity supply/demand. Impending commercial startup of BHP's low-cost Jansen mine (Stage 1 in 2027, Stage 2 in 2031 adding 8.5 Mtpa) poses a structural supply shock.
